title: HHS-04: recommendation identity held for one-to-many mapping
summary: HHS-04 remains In Review because the Phase 56P local action combines 2 distinct official recommendations in GAO-24-106276.
key_findings: Phase 56P action: HHS should better manage fragmentation in department-wide after-action programs used to identify and resolve recurring emergency-response challenges.
Official identity: held; no single official recommendation identity assigned.
Affected component: Department of Health and Human Services; Secretary.
Current GAO status: Open – Partially Addressed; status period: January 2026.

Agency response: HHS developed standard operating procedures. GAO is awaiting evidence from an exercise or response after-action report before determining whether either recommendation is implemented.
Continuation rule: Preserve HHS-04 as the parent local action and create recommendation-specific child records before publication; do not collapse Recommendations 1 and 2.
why_it_matters: The crosswalk replaces a letter-level local reference with an inspectable official report-and-recommendation identity where the evidence supports exactly one match.
ftfn_relevance: Preserves local action key HHS-04 as a crosswalk rather than an official identifier.
Separates official recommendation identity, affected entity, GAO status, agency response, implementation evidence, closure, and outcome.

Preserves both candidates: GAO-24-106276 Recommendation 1: Coordinate after-action work across HHS component agencies and integrate existing component programs. | GAO-24-106276 Recommendation 2: Include relevant external stakeholders in each emergency-response after-action process.
evidence_limits: An agency response, concurrence, planned date, submission, or artifact under review does not by itself establish implementation or closure.
GAO recommendation status is not interchangeable with the Phase 56F entity evidence state.
Recommendation closure would not by itself establish operating performance, readiness, safety, value, or causation.
A one-to-many local-action mapping cannot be published as one official recommendation identity.
